environment.tool: manual audit of the tag source + live compiled binary; raw socket range matrix with measured byte counts

findings.description: The cap check is on the GET path only; a HEAD request returns before it. A 67108865-byte file answers HEAD with 200 and a Content-Length it can never deliver, while GET is 403: a client that preflights with HEAD, or any link checker or monitoring probe that uses HEAD, sees a healthy resource that cannot actually be fetched. Precondition: a file one byte over the 64 MiB cap.
findings.title: The 64 MiB body cap is checked after the HEAD early return, so HEAD reports 200 for a file whose GET is 403

findings.description: The cap compares the computed body length, not the file size, so Range: bytes=0-67108863 on a 67108865-byte file computes exactly the cap, passes the gate, and returns 206 with the first 64 MiB. The same file with no Range, or with bytes=0-67108864, is 403. Precondition: a file over the cap and an attacker-chosen Range.
findings.title: An explicit Content-Length range of exactly the cap bypasses the cap gate and serves a file that a plain GET refuses

findings.description: The 403 is emitted with Connection: close, so a pipelined successor behind the oversized-file request is dropped exactly as with any other closing response. Recorded for composition, not as a new defect. Precondition: pipelining plus an over-cap file.
findings.title: A 403 from the cap closes mid-pipeline and eats the following request

limitations: Cap findings need a file at or over 64 MiB
